title: Wherever you go, karma goes with you
odia: ଗଙ୍ଗା ଯା ଗୟା ଯା କର୍ମ ଘେନି ବୁଲୁଥା।
literal_meaning: Go to the Ganga, go to Gaya; keep wandering with your karma.
meaning_odia: ଗଙ୍ଗାକୁ ଯାଅ କି ଗୟାକୁ ଯାଅ, ନିଜ କର୍ମ ସାଙ୍ଗରେ ରହିଥାଏ। ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ସବୁ କ୍ଷେତ୍ରରେ କର୍ମର ପ୍ରାଧାନ୍ୟ କହେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ସ୍ଥାନ ବଦଳାଇଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ନିଜ କର୍ମ ଓ ତାହାର ପରିଣାମକୁ ପଛରେ ଛାଡ଼ି ଯାଇହୁଏ ନାହିଁ।
explanation: The repeated invitation to go offers two sacred destinations, then adds what the traveller carries everywhere: karma. The inspected source gloss stresses its continuing importance. Our editorial reading hears a reminder that a change of place does not by itself separate a person from their deeds and consequences.
usage_example: Original imagined example: A reader discussing the verse says that changing one’s surroundings is not the same as addressing the consequences of earlier actions. The saying supplies the image of something carried along on every journey.
cultural_context: Ganga and Gaya place the journey in a pilgrimage frame. The short repeated ଯା gives movement to the opening, while ଘେନି makes karma something that travels with the person. The verse’s force rests on that contrast between changing destinations and a continuing companion.
